info.name: Airline microservices - all APIs
info.description:
Every API of every service, through the API gateway (or straight to each service).

**Folders**
- **A. Full flow**: run first, top to bottom. Creates the data the other folders use: accounts, airline, flight, fares, a booking, a payment, tickets.
- **B. All APIs by service**: every endpoint of every service. Each folder adds its own test data, tests it, and deletes it again.
- **C. Gateway, Eureka and security checks**.
- **D. Clean-up**: cancels the flow's flight and deletes the airline. Run last.

**Environments**
- *Airline - via gateway*: everything through http://localhost:8080. Use this with Docker.
- *Airline - direct to services*: each service on its own port (8081, 8002, 5004, ...). Use this when the services run locally (IDE / mvn).

Both have the direct URLs for the `/internal/**` requests (the gateway blocks those).

**Before you start**
1. Start the system (`PAYMENT_ABA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9 docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d`, or the services locally).
2. Import the collection and both environments; pick one; fill in **adminEmail** / **adminPassword** (ADMIN_EMAIL / ADMIN_PASSWORD in services/user-service/.env).
3. Send *A. Full flow* top to bottom (or use the Runner).

**Manual steps**
- After a sign-up, put its 6-digit code into **ownerOtp** / **customerOtp** / **tmpOtp** / **resetOtp** (user-service log with MAIL_ENABLED=false, else the inbox).
- The simulated ABA payment and the `/internal/**` requests need the services' own ports: they work with the *direct* setup; in Docker use the command in the request's description.
- Requests marked ⚠ *Calls ABA PayWay* only work once ABA is connected.

Each run makes a new owner, airline, flight and customer (the `run` variable), so it can be run again and again.

item.name: 7. Payment
item.description: The payment is created for real. ABA isn't connected, so its "paid" callback is simulated.

request.description:
Creates the payment and the PayWay checkout form. ABA isn't called.

*POST /api/v1/payments, as customer.*

What payment-service tells booking-service after ABA confirms a payment. **Internal endpoint:** the gateway blocks /internal/**, so this goes straight to the service ({{bookingDirect}}). Works when the services run locally (IDE / mvn); in Docker the services have no host port.

**In Docker**, run this in a terminal instead (fill in the two numbers):

```
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml exec booking-service curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8066/internal/v1/bookings/BOOKING_ID/payment-result -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"paymentId": PAYMENT_ID, "status": "SUCCESS"}'
```

*POST /internal/v1/bookings/{{bookingId}}/payment-result, no login.*

exec: t.forEach((x, i) => { pm.collectionVariables.set("ticketId" + (i + 1), x.id); pm.collectionVariables.set("ticketNumber" + (i + 1), x.ticketNumber); });
pm.test("3 places booked (goes through the outbox: resend after a few seconds if 0)", () => pm.expect(c.bookedSeats).to.eql(3));

item.name: B. All APIs by service
item.description: Every endpoint, service by service. Needs A. Full flow first (it uses its ids and tokens).

request.description:
Waits 60 s between codes: sent right after the sign-up it answers 429.

*POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email/resend, no login.*

Needs the 6-digit code that was just sent. With MAIL_ENABLED=false it's in the user-service log: `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml logs user-service | grep 'DEV EMAIL'` (or the inbox). Put it in the **tmpOtp** environment variable first.

*POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email, no login.*

Swaps the refresh token for a new access token (and a new refresh token).

*POST /api/v1/auth/refresh, no login.*

Sends a reset code. Same answer whether or not the email exists.

*POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password, no login.*

Needs the 6-digit code that was just sent. With MAIL_ENABLED=false it's in the user-service log: `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml logs user-service | grep 'DEV EMAIL'` (or the inbox). Put it in the **resetOtp** environment variable first.

*POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password, no login.*

request.description:
⚠ **Calls ABA PayWay.** Only works once ABA PayWay is connected (real merchant id / API key, and PAYMENT_ABA_BASE_URL pointing at ABA). With the test setup (ABA pointed at an unreachable address) it fails.

*POST /api/v1/payments, as customer.*

⚠ **Calls ABA PayWay.** Only works once ABA PayWay is connected (real merchant id / API key, and PAYMENT_ABA_BASE_URL pointing at ABA). With the test setup (ABA pointed at an unreachable address) it fails.

*POST /api/v1/payments/{{paymentId}}/sync, as customer.*

⚠ **Calls ABA PayWay.** Only works once ABA PayWay is connected (real merchant id / API key, and PAYMENT_ABA_BASE_URL pointing at ABA). With the test setup (ABA pointed at an unreachable address) it fails. Also needs ABA's RSA key (ABA_RSA_PUBLIC_KEY).

*POST /api/v1/payments/{{paymentId}}/refunds, as admin.*

item.name: ABA's callback (what ABA sends after a payment)

request.description:
ABA posts this when a customer pays; payment-service then checks the payment with ABA before accepting it. ⚠ **Calls ABA PayWay.** Only works once ABA PayWay is connected (real merchant id / API key, and PAYMENT_ABA_BASE_URL pointing at ABA). With the test setup (ABA pointed at an unreachable address) it fails.

*POST /api/v1/payments/aba/callback, no login.*

What booking-service sends when a paid booking is cancelled. This booking was never paid, so nothing is refunded. **Internal endpoint:** the gateway blocks /internal/**, so this goes straight to the service ({{paymentDirect}}). Works when the services run locally (IDE / mvn); in Docker the services have no host port.

*POST /internal/v1/payments/refunds, no login.*
